notes:
VERDICT: FAIL. faultFixed = false.

The named fault was two-part and only the sign was corrected. The render is no longer portrait, so the literal inversion is gone - but the target was stated explicitly as 1.2:1 and the render lands at 2.85:1, which is 2.32x off. The previous attempt was 1.74x off in the opposite direction. Measured as error magnitude, this attempt is worse than the one it was meant to fix. Same failure mode as the last two rounds: the correction was followed in direction but not in magnitude.

WHAT I MEASURED AND HOW
- Drawn markers extracted by red mask (R>110, R-G>55, R-B>55), two connected components, 6192 and 6175 px. Each fitted as a quadrilateral in its OWN rotated frame: the two vertical strokes fitted only over rows where both clusters are under 26 px wide (so the bottom bar cannot contaminate the fit - an earlier unconstrained fit gave a spurious 62 px horizontal drift and a bogus 1.04 aspect), and the bar fitted over the middle 50 percent of the span. Branch tops taken from the topmost red row of each stroke individually (669 for the inner, 679 for the outer), not a shared value.
- Rendered welts fitted the same way: base by minimum high-pass response per column, verticals by maximum |d/dx| of high-pass.
- SPAN CHECKED (discipline item 2): the rendered base line carries response below -8 continuously from x=676 to x=812 on the right and x=69 to x=189 on the left, dying off within 8 px of the fitted corner intersections at 681/816.9 and 66.2/193.8. The fit is not truncated.
- SATURATION CHECKED (item 3): each vertical was searched in a 22 px window and the located line sat interior to it; each vertical's extent was then re-scanned over a 100 px y-range and confirmed to start and stop inside that range (right-outer branch response jumps 13 -> 23 at y=630 and dies at y=692; right-inner jumps 18 -> 93 at y=670 and dies at y=722). Neither is measuring its own box.
- LANDMARK VALIDATED (item 4): bag depth = waistband lower seam to the lowest point of the flipped-out bag, traced independently in both images by column brightness steps in the render and by ink-run scans in the drawing. Drawing 506 px, render 472/480 px. Bag proportions themselves match well (bag width/depth 0.433 drawn vs 0.440 rendered), which is what makes the ratios comparable at all. This landmark differs from the 620 px used in the previous verdict; 620 spans the waistband as well and is not the bag.
- WRONG-EDGE CHECK (item 6): my first read of the left welt appeared to show a fourth, top side. It does not exist - that line is the pocket bag's own internal fold seam crossing the region (it passes x~76 at y=634 on the fitted fold trajectory). Directional gradient probing along the hypothetical top edge returned 6-16 against a plain-cloth control of 4-14. I discarded the false reading.

SUMMARY TABLE (drawing -> render)
  aspect W/D          1.21  ->  2.85          (2.32x too wide-for-depth)  FAIL
  depth / bag depth   0.233 ->  0.099         (43 percent of target)      FAIL
  width / bag depth   0.281 ->  0.282         (0.4 percent off)           PASS
  bottom edge seat    0.882 ->  0.882         (exact)                     PASS
  top edge seat       0.658 ->  0.780         (consequence of depth)      FAIL
  horizontal centre   0.505 ->  0.486         (2 points off)              PASS
  base tilt           9.5/9.8 deg -> 10.7 deg (1.2 deg off)               PASS
  count / sides       2, one per bag -> 2, one per bag                    PASS

THE SINGLE ACTIONABLE FIX: the width, the seat, the tilt and the topology are all correct. Only the depth is wrong, and it is wrong by a clean factor. Pin the base line and lengthen both branches by 2.3x - to roughly 110 px in this render, giving a top edge at 0.66 of bag depth. Every other number should come out unchanged.

NOT MEASURABLE - the drawing carries no printed dimension callouts, so no centimetre figure is recoverable for the coin pocket. Every number above is a pixel measurement or a dimensionless ratio against the bag landmark. I also could not compare thread colour, stitch density or fabric hand against the drawing, which is a plain line drawing and carries none of that information; those were not scored against the blueprint.

BLUEPRINT COLLISION - RE-CONFIRMED BY HASH, and this is a catalog defect, not an image defect. public/images/blueprints/remote/7f475092fe8b__3532.jpg (coin-both) and public/images/blueprints/factory/88f95280e442__3532__Left_right.jpg (watch-both) are byte-identical: md5 87658726bf98f5322cbc719704c23291, 61437 bytes each. I verified in data-store/options/trousers.json that sections[0].fields[3].options[3] (watch-both, "Both Sides") and sections[0].fields[4].options[3] (coin-both, "Both Sides") reference them respectively. One drawing therefore backs two different craft options with markers in the same position, so the illustration alone CANNOT distinguish a coin pocket from a watch pocket - and no amount of fidelity to it will make the two catalog images differ. That needs a data fix upstream before this option can ever be considered genuinely correct, independent of anything the photography does.

I made no writes to data-store/, public/images/generated/, or .craft-pipeline/. All working files went to the session scratchpad only.
